items.title: NHTSA Opens Probe Into 1.2 Million Ford Vehicles Over Burn Risk from Airbag
items.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is investigating certain Ford vehicles over reports of burn injuries caused by airbag deployments.

items.title: Can OnStar and Super Cruise Drive GM's Digital Revenue Growth?
items.summary: General Motors is growing its recurring software business as OnStar subscriptions and Super Cruise adoption rise, opening new revenue opportunities.

items.title: Ford Yields Nearly 5%. GM Is Buying Back $20 Billion in Stock. Which Is Better?
items.summary: Two automakers posted Q3 results, then sent shareholders in opposite directions: one keeps mailing checks while the other shrinks its share count. For retirees counting on income, the safer-looking choice may not be the obvious one.

items.title: Can GM's Next-Generation Pickups Support Growth in 2027?
items.summary: General Motors' next-generation 2027 Silverado and Sierra feature upgraded engines and premium trims, positioning it for richer product mix and profitability.

items.title: Car shoppers hunt for a bargain, yet pickups remain immune to inflation
items.summary: Auto sales tell a tale of two markets as pricey truck sales soar, just as more car shoppers look at certified pre-owned cars.

items.title: Trump Gives Automakers a Fuel-Economy Break, and GM Is Siding With Him
items.summary: Key TakeawaysAn industry group including GM, Ford, Toyota and Volkswagen backed the Trump administration in court over a rollback that cuts the 2031 fuel-economy target to 34. 9 mpg from 50.

items.title: GM Slides 7% From a 52-Week High as New York Files Its $220 Million Driver Data Settlement
items.summary: Key TakeawaysGeneral Motors fell 7% in two days from a 52-week high as New York filed its share of a $220 million driver data settlement. New York’s attorney general said GM’s OnStar app told more than 370,000 drivers they weren’t enrolled while GM collected and sold their data.

items.title: Ford's stock rises, GM's falls for week ending Nov. 6
items.summary: Ford saw its stock price rise while stock in General Motors and Stellantis fell for the week ending Nov. 6.
